lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: Clover again? I wanted to plant corn!

lines.speaker: kernel
lines.text: Me too. But this soil leaves me hungry.

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: Hungry for nitrogen! Every crop needs it.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: But the air is full of nitrogen!

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: Plants can't use it like that. Follow me!

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: Clover roots have little bumps, full of bacteria called rhizobia.

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: They pull nitrogen from the air, and turn it into ammonia.

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: When the clover dies, its nitrogen is released into the soil.

lines.speaker: kernel
lines.text: Hey! How did you get so tall?

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: The clover fed the soil, for the next crop!

lines.speaker: wiggs
lines.text: That's why many farmers rotate clover through their fields.
